title: HTTP CONNECT-IP: dissect IP in HTTP/3 datagrams
description:
This MR introduces Context ID and IP packet dissection inside HTTP/3 datagrams for CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484).

CONNECT-IP is quite different from other IP encapsulations dissected today:
- Single HTTP/3 packet may contain multiple HTTP/3 datagrams with IP packets
- Encapsulated IP packet may also contain HTTP/3 which creates multiple layers of IP/UDP/QUIC/TLS/HTTP3 within a single packet

Proposed approach creates a new `packet_info` and `frame_data`, stores per-frame data (`pfd`) in HTTP/3 stream specific dissector state and creates a new sequence for packet/frame numbers. Is that an acceptable path or should I try something else? If this is an acceptable approach should the relevant code go into a more generic place as few other encapsulations may need similar logic (standard CONNECT in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, CONNECT-UDP in all HTTP versions and the upcoming Templated CONNECT-TCP in all HTTP versions).

Hi,

Can you share some pcap ?

[connect-ip.pcapng](/uploads/b0cbd3eee6e1a856493bcd012eb6daee/connect-ip.pcapng)

Attached file contains a bunch of ICMP in CONNECT-IP (packets 41-139), SSH in CONNECT-IP (packets 146-420) and HTTPS in CONNECT-IP (packets 423-451).

Packet capture intentionally has massively reduced inner MTU (500 bytes) and quite a bit of inner re-ordering to check reassembly. TLS secrets for outer QUIC and inner HTTPS are included in the pcapng.

Since everything seems to be working correctly, I'm dropping my funky logic to introduce new sequence of frame/packet numbers. The only potential issue I can think of is reordered HTTP/3 datagrams within a single QUIC packet, but that's not very realistic. Separate tracking of `pfd` is still necessary.

Removing "draft" from this MR as everything seems to be working correctly now.

Once this and https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21032 is merged, I'm happy to tackle HTTP capsules.

Have you looked at other tunnelling protocol examples?  I'm not sure creating a new packet_info structure is the way to go...

I looked at [https://wiki.wireshark.org/uploads/__moin_import__/attachments/SampleCaptures/pim-reg.cap](pim-reg.cap) that tunnels IPv6 and it has the same "display" problem as the connect-ip capture above.  I would say the issue is and should be fixed in the IP dissector and NOT the high layer dissector.  This is a "workaround" that will lead to more subtle bugs later on.

This is not about IP address conflict. One packet can have multiple HTTP/3 datagrams with CONNECT-IP packets inside them. State of dissectors will be messed up if the same protocol (such as TLS) is present in both outer packet and multiple inner packets.
The same challenge will arise in HTTP/2 CONNECT and HTTP/3 CONNECT as a single packet can contain multiple streams with inner Data frames.

My point is that the "layering problem" shouldn't be handled at the higher layer dissector.  The behavior you describe is a limitation of the IP or TLS dissector and affects any tunnelling protocols/dissectors.  It should not try to be solved/worked around at the HTTP CONNECT layer.
Pinfo->layer is ment to aid in distinguishing several occurrences of the same protocol in a frame.

CONNECT-IP is quite different from other encapsulations implemented in Wireshark today in a way that one can have multiple independent "instances" of the same protocol inside a single packet. Dissectors store their state using `_proto_data`. Without creating a separate state for `pinfo->fd->pfd` and `pinfo->proto_data` every stateful dissector breaks.
Wireguard, GRE, IPinIP, etc. can have one and only one encapsulated packet. CONNECT-IP can have many encapsulated IP packets in HTTP/3 datagrams within one HTTP/3 packet.
I am all for having a generic solution that will work not only for CONNECT-IP but also for other cases with occurrences of the same protocol - but it does not seem to exist yet.
I'm not sure that layer will help here as there is no strict hierarchical layering here. Multiple HTTP/3 datagrams travelling inside a single HTTP/3 packet are on the same "layer" - yet dissector instances must have independent state from each other.
Cache the handle from in the _handoff function so you only have to find it once.
Not sure if I follow. Can you please elaborate?
There are numerous examples, but look at packet-wireguard.c in how it handles calling the IP dissector.
You can use GUINT_TO_POINTER() for the key and not have to allocate additional memory.

I don't think `GUINT_TO_POINTER` works for `uint64_t`.
Key is 64-bit: 32-bit of `pinfo->num` and 32-bit for offset from the `tvb_offset_from_real_beginning`.
I don't believe we support 32-bit platforms anymore and the size of the key is a void*, which should be 64-bit.

On my system it's:
#define GUINT_TO_POINTER(u)	((gpointer) (guint64) (u))
I would also consider not squashing 2 32-bit values together as those could (eventually) expand to be 64-bit values themselves.
I agree. Any suggestions how to construct a key for storing `pfds` specific to the datagram?

Recommend using expert_add_info on the returned proto_item* from the proto_tree_add_item_ret_varint call above so Wireshark can properly highlight the incorrect field.  And if you're not going to use printf-style arguments in your message, you can just have the expected text in ei_http_datagram_unknown_context_id.
Will do!
